name: Volunteer organizer's personal backlog
scenario: A part-time volunteer records sporadic personal and neighborhood tasks between work commitments. Several action verbs recur across unrelated tasks. There is no prior baseline for the two most specialized chores.

tasks.title: File the bus receipts
tasks.description: Photograph four receipts, check the dates on the existing expense sheet, and send the completed claim.
tasks.details: I have all four in my bag and know the reimbursement template.

tasks.title: Check the new walk-to-school route
tasks.description: Walk the route once, mark two temporary crossings and send a corrected meeting location to parents.
tasks.details: Meet at the library door. The new construction fencing has blocked the usual crossing.

tasks.title: Sort the winter concert photos
tasks.description: Choose ten images for the neighborhood archive, rename them with dates and copy them into the shared folder.
tasks.details: The phone sorted them into one album already. Skip blurred group shots.

tasks.title: Check the postcard proof
tasks.description: Verify the venue name, door time and spelling on the printer proof and approve the corrected copy.
tasks.details: I can compare it to the previous flyer. The printer already placed the logo.

tasks.title: Return the allotment gate key
tasks.description: Match the tag against the access list, hand the key to the coordinator, and record the return.
tasks.details: Coordinator will be at the site after lunch. My timer covers the handover and paperwork.

tasks.title: Resolve a duplicate travel claim
tasks.description: Reconcile one duplicate bank entry against two electronic receipts and amend the reimbursement sheet.
tasks.details: I need to check one disputed date; the rest of the trip is already entered.

tasks.title: Sort the book donation boxes
tasks.description: Check the posted acceptance list, separate torn items and label each box for the library sale.
tasks.details: Three open boxes, one volunteer table. I can use last year's category labels.

tasks.title: Refresh the Saturday helper roster
tasks.description: Check availability replies from five returning volunteers and send each person a station and arrival time.
tasks.details: Copy last month's roster. Everyone has worked at the event before.

holdouts.title: Digitize a cassette for the neighborhood archive
holdouts.description: Transfer both sides of one cassette to WAV, locate six spoken introductions, and label each cut for the archive.
holdouts.details: First time doing a cassette transfer. The existing photo album uses the same archive name. The audio equipment is borrowed.

pdf.title: Oral history transfer sheet: rehearsal cassette

sections.heading: Source
sections.body: One home-recorded cassette marked Side A and Side B. The introductions are spoken over room noise. Side B begins partway through a rehearsal. No digital copy or timings are available.

sections.heading: Delivery
sections.body: Transfer both sides at normal playback speed. Keep a full continuous WAV for each side and a separate text cue sheet. Identify the six spoken introductions by listening; preserve gaps and uncertain names.

sections.heading: Quality check
sections.body: Before returning the deck, listen across the side change, verify the two WAV files open, and compare cue positions against the introductions. Mark any clipped announcements for a second pass.

holdouts.check: Tests an unseen category with a misleading archive keyword. A conservative cold-start estimate or low-confidence match is appropriate.

holdouts.title: Prepare the first street closure permit packet
holdouts.description: Read the permit checklist, assemble a scaled route map and accessibility notes, and check that both event sites are represented.
holdouts.details: First closure permit for this group. Previous event approvals were printer proofs. Leave the two organizer signatures blank.

pdf.title: Temporary street use: draft applicant checklist

sections.heading: Map requirement
sections.body: Include both assembly sites, the segment to be closed, crossings that remain open and the path around the closure. Mark each access point clearly enough for a reviewer to identify it without accompanying photographs.

sections.heading: Access plan
sections.body: Describe how deliveries and mobility-device users will reach the open storefronts. The map and text must use matching site names. Identify the organizer responsible for checking access at each end.

sections.heading: Submission packet
sections.body: Bundle the map, access plan and two unsigned organizer blocks into one PDF. Check page order and cross-references. Site inspection and official processing happen later and are outside this preparation task.

holdouts.check: Tests broad same-category fallback on a specialized first-time application; similarities to routine approval or reimbursement tasks should be questioned.
